@Werkov 
> Given the kernel's default BFQ weight is 100, there's an asymmetry between the minimum and maximum weights ratio to this baseline. Therefore, I think the correct formula should remap only the upper "half" of the range:
> 
> ```
> if (weight <= 100)
>     kernel_weight = weight;
> else
>     kernel_weight = 100 + (weight - 100) / 11;
> ```
> 
> so that units with the default config would still yield the `kernel_weight` of 100. (But at the same time the kernel asymmetry seems a bit arbitrary to me, might be better fixed in BFQ.)
> 
> EDIT: Note that the asymmetry is present both in v1 and v2 BFQ cgroup API.

Could you give me a reference for that?

urks, bfq. we should have never merged support for that mess. systemd should not be the place to work around kernel politics.

And it sucks we always make two writes to these files, of which one then fails.

@Werkov Thanks.

I may mis-understand the issue. Is value `{blkio,io}.bfq.weight` propagated to `{blkio,io}.weight`?? So, we should first set the value to `bfq.weight`, and then to `weight`?
Updated. PTAL.

This pull request **introduces 1 alert** when merging a2f702be80fd7fa80294117224a5ae28addb238b into e243d78c30f4ac27d8abf56f02f95a4359eba305 - [view on LGTM.com](https://lgtm.com/projects/g/systemd/systemd/rev/pr-4fb6d0e7d51faa7d96344db3a312a9b18356c1a3)

**new alerts:**

* 1 for FIXME comment

TL;DR Write verbatim weights into (`io.weight`, `io.bfq.weight`) or `blkio.bfq.weight`.

There are two aspects to this PR:
   1. what attribute files are written,
   2. what is the written value.

Currently, there is no propagation of values between BFQ or iocost weights. The safest workaround is to write both variants to be independent on the used policy (on v2). There is only `blkio.bfq.weight` and no `blkio.weight` (used to be CFQ) on v1 since kernel v5.0, so in that case it's enough to write `blkio.bfq.weight` only (unless pre-v5.0 compatibility is intended).

The actual value, on second (and third) thought, I think no transformation is the best approach. The old formula confuses users (the reported behavior in #20519 works as "intended" actually) and the new one won't be much better I'm afraid. (I [propose](https://lore.kernel.org/linux-block/20210826131212.GE4520@blackbody.suse.cz/T/#m632fd3e33722574543044b980286bcfdf3fcedaa) that BFQ accepts the >1000 values too.)
I added the helper as suggested by Lennart and a few test cases to make sure that the conversion happens as expected (it does). I force-pushed into your branch to speed things up.

Are you displeased by the backwards goto or the repeated write in general?

(The "propagation" sentence is dropped from the message of the first commit.)

The cause is that there are two policies for proportional IO control, systemd provides one abstraction on top of these (which is IMO good). (See also [above](https://github.com/systemd/systemd/pull/20522#issuecomment-906423513) what differs.)

> Are you displeased by the backwards goto or the repeated write in general?

The repeated write. Looping is nasty, and usually causes trouble sooner or later.

I think the approach in this PR is good: we scale the value and provide a uniform API. I don't think the details of the scaling are terribly important: we provide a reasonable linear mapping and that should be good enough.

O.K. Let's move forward with that.
Some [debug messages](https://github.com/systemd/systemd/pull/21728) may come handy when troubleshooting.

issue_context.title: IOWeight= doesn't set io.bfq.weight
issue_context.body:
**systemd version the issue has been seen with**
 > v249.2-1.fc35

<!-- **NOTE:** Do not submit bug reports about anything but the two most recently released *major* systemd versions upstream! -->
<!--           If there have been multiple stable releases for that major version, please consider updating to a recent one before reporting an issue. -->
<!--           When using a distro package, please make sure that the version reported is meaningful for upstream. -->
<!-- See https://github.com/systemd/systemd-stable/releases for the list of most recent releases. -->
<!-- For older version please use distribution trackers (see https://systemd.io/CONTRIBUTING#filing-issues). -->

**Used distribution**
 > Fedora Rawhide

**Linux kernel version used** (`uname -a`)
<!-- Make sure to enclose the pasted kernel version in `backticks`, so that
     GitHub doesn't convert the `#` character typically included in it into a
     reference to old GitHub issues. -->
 > `5.14.0-0.rc5.20210813gitf8e6dfc64f61.46.fc36.x86_64`

**CPU architecture issue was seen on**
 > x86_64

Since https://github.com/systemd/systemd/pull/13335 `IOWeight=` set also the `io.bfq.weight` cgroup property. However, in recent systemd versions this is no longer true:

```
# systemd-run -u test.service -p IOWeight=666 /bin/sleep infinity
Running as unit: test.service
# systemctl show -p IOWeight test.service
IOWeight=666
# cat /sys/fs/cgroup/system.slice/test.service/io.bfq.weight 
default 67
```

Example from Fedora 33 (v246.10-1.fc33, 5.11.9-200.fc33.x86_64):
```
# systemd-run -u test.service -p IOWeight=666 /bin/sleep infinity
Running as unit: test.service
# systemctl show -p IOWeight test.service
IOWeight=666
# cat /sys/fs/cgroup/system.slice/test.service/io.bfq.weight 
default 666
```

/cc @keszybz
